name: Photon
what_it_is: A multiplayer development platform offering networking engines, voice and chat services, and cloud hosting for games and other applications.
platforms: Cross-platform per the page: mobile, PC, consoles and VR/AR, with cross-play across its multiplayer SDKs. Unity is named for Quantum.
pricing: Not published on the homepage. It has a 'Try Photon free' sign-up link and mentions cost-effective pricing plans without figures.
key_features: Voice with 3D audio and noise reduction
notable: Homepage claims over 1.4 billion monthly players in its global Photon Cloud
Homepage logos include Vodafone, Daimler, Adobe and Airbus

facts.fact: Photon's homepage describes it as a multiplayer development platform with networking engines, voice and chat services, and cloud hosting.
The homepage does not publish prices; it links to a 'Try Photon free' sign-up and mentions cost-effective pricing plans without figures.
The homepage claims over 1.4 billion monthly players in its global Photon Cloud.

name: Mirror
what_it_is: Open source networking library for Unity.
pricing: Not stated on the page. The page calls Mirror open source and links to a Unity Asset Store download.
notable: Source code is on GitHub at vis2k/Mirror, linked from the homepage
Docs are hosted on GitBook

facts.fact: Mirror's homepage describes it as open source networking for Unity.
The homepage calls Mirror open source and links to a Unity Asset Store download; no license name or price is stated on the page.
The homepage links to documentation at mirror-networking.gitbook.io/docs and to the source on GitHub.

name: Netcode for GameObjects
what_it_is: Unity's netcode library for multiplayer games, aimed at casual co-op games and including a Distributed Authority mode, part of Unity's multiplayer services.
platforms: Not stated on the page; the page says Unity supports 25+ platforms without listing them.
pricing: Not stated on this page. It links to a 'View pricing' page for gaming services.
notable: The page positions Netcode for GameObjects for casual co-op games and Netcode for Entities for competitive action games
The page links docs for Netcode for GameObjects version 2.7

facts.fact: Unity's multiplayer page describes Netcode for GameObjects as aimed at casual co-op games and includes a Distributed Authority mode.
The page does not state prices for Netcode for GameObjects; it links to a 'View pricing' page for Unity gaming services.
The page is published by Unity Technologies, per its copyright line.

name: Fish-Networking
what_it_is: A free, server-authoritative networking solution for Unity (FishNet).
pricing: Free. The page describes it as a free networking solution with no CCU caps or CCU paywalls.
notable: No CCU caps or CCU paywalls, per the page
Documentation on GitBook, source on GitHub

facts.fact: The FishNet documentation describes it as an original free and versatile networking solution for Unity.
The page states there are no CCU caps and no CCU paywalls.
The page links the source code on GitHub at FirstGearGames/FishNet.

name: Normcore
what_it_is: A multiplayer networking solution for Unity, with Normcore Public and Normcore Private product lines.
platforms: Unity; desktop and console, mobile, VR and AR, and WebGL
pricing: 'Start developing for free.' Pay only for what you use, with no hidden fees or CCU caps. Plan prices are not stated; a 'Contact Sales' button is present.
notable: The page says it scales automatically to millions of users
Offers Private Cloud and On-Premises Hosting options

facts.fact: Normcore is a multiplayer networking solution for Unity, published by Normal VR LLC in Brooklyn, NY, per the copyright line.
The page says developers can start for free and pay only for what they use, with no hidden fees or CCU caps; plan prices are not stated.
The page offers Private Cloud and On-Premises Hosting options and Enterprise Support.

name: Colyseus
what_it_is: An open-source real-time multiplayer framework for Node.js, with built-in matchmaking, state sync and client SDKs.
platforms: Server runs on Node.js. Client SDKs for TypeScript/JavaScript, Unity, Godot (Alpha), GameMaker (Alpha), Defold, Haxe, C (Alpha) and Construct 3; Cocos Creator also mentioned.
pricing: The framework is free and MIT licensed. Colyseus Cloud starts at $15/mo.
notable: MIT licensed; the page says free forever, even for commercial games
Colyseus Cloud is offered across 32 global locations

facts.fact: Colyseus's homepage describes it as an open-source real-time multiplayer framework for Node.js with matchmaking, state sync and client SDKs.
The homepage says the framework is MIT licensed and free forever, even for commercial games; Colyseus Cloud starts at $15/mo.
The homepage says the server can be deployed to AWS, Google Cloud, DigitalOcean, Fly.io, Railway or bare metal.

name: coherence
what_it_is: A multiplayer SDK and hosting platform for Unity games.
platforms: Unity. Hosting can be cloud, peer-to-peer, self-managed or hybrid.
pricing: No plan prices are shown on the homepage. It has a 'Start for free' button and a 'What does coherence cost?' FAQ whose answer is not shown; the pricing policy is linked under Legal.
notable: Customer logos on the homepage include Devolver Digital and LEGO
Case studies include Vampire Survivors and Lost Skies

facts.fact: coherence describes itself on its homepage as the simplest way to build and host multiplayer games with Unity.
The homepage has a 'Start for free' button, but no plan prices are shown; the 'What does coherence cost?' FAQ answer is not visible.
The homepage names Devolver Digital and LEGO among its customer logos.

name: SpacetimeDB
what_it_is: A reactive backend platform that combines a database, server logic, auth, deployment and real-time sync.
platforms: Server logic in Rust, C# or TypeScript; quickstarts for Node.js, Bun, Deno, HTML5, React, Vue, Next.js and others; cloud deployment.
pricing: No pricing terms on the homepage; a pricing page is linked.
key_features: Role-based access control and single sign-on
notable: Homepage logos include Google, Supercell, Databricks, PayPal and Stripe
Starter templates include Team Chat, Party Game and Card Game

facts.fact: The homepage describes Spacetime as a reactive backend platform combining database, server logic, auth, deployment and real-time sync.
The footer says Spacetime is designed and engineered by Clockwork Labs.
The homepage gives no pricing terms and links to a separate pricing page.

name: Edgegap
what_it_is: An automated game server hosting and orchestration service for any engine and service.
platforms: 615+ locations and 17+ cloud providers per the page; engines named include Unreal, Unity, Godot, Nakama, Mirror, Photon Fusion, PurrNet and Fish-Networking; also cloud gaming, mobile, VR and web games.
pricing: Pay per minute on edge cloud with no upfront costs or fixed monthly fees. No specific prices on the homepage; a pricing calculator is linked.
notable: Page claims 615+ locations across 17+ providers
Customers named on the page include Halfbrick Studios and Starbreeze AB

facts.fact: The homepage describes Edgegap as an automated game server hosting and orchestration service for any engine and service.
The homepage says there are no upfront costs or fixed monthly fees and that customers pay per minute on edge cloud; specific prices are not listed.
The homepage names Halfbrick Studios and Starbreeze AB among its customers.

name: Hathora
drop_reason: NOT GATHERED: hathora.dev returns a 301 redirect to gamefabric.com, and the WebFetch safety check for that domain was rate-limited, so the new site was not opened. Rerun before use; this is not a vendor drop.

name: Amazon GameLift
what_it_is: A fully managed AWS service with game streaming and multiplayer game server capabilities (GameLift Servers and GameLift Streams).
platforms: GameLift Streams works on any device with a browser; GameLift Servers platforms are not stated. Streaming up to 1080p at 60 frames per second.
pricing: No GameLift-specific pricing on the page; it links to general AWS pricing and the AWS Pricing Calculator. Free network bandwidth on eligible instances is stated for GameLift Servers.
key_features: Game streaming up to 1080p at 60 fps
notable: Autoscaling can launch up to 9,000 game servers per minute (page claim)
FlexMatch connects up to 200 players per game session

facts.fact: The AWS page describes Amazon GameLift as a fully managed service with game streaming and multiplayer game server capabilities, provided by Amazon Web Services, Inc.
The page links only general AWS pricing pages and the AWS Pricing Calculator; no GameLift-specific prices are shown.
The page states autoscaling can launch up to 9,000 game servers per minute and FlexMatch connects up to 200 players per game session.

name: Agones
what_it_is: An open source platform to host, run and scale dedicated game servers on Kubernetes.
platforms: Runs on Kubernetes, anywhere Kubernetes can run; includes an SDK for engine integration.
pricing: Open source; no pricing. The license is not stated on the page.
notable: Described on the page as a Cloud Native Computing Foundation sandbox project
Latest release listed on the page is 1.62.0

facts.fact: The Agones homepage describes it as an open source platform to host, run and scale dedicated game servers on Kubernetes.
The homepage describes Agones as a Cloud Native Computing Foundation sandbox project and carries an LF Projects, LLC copyright line.
The homepage lists version 1.62.0 as the newest release in its release menu.

name: Gameye
what_it_is: A game server orchestration platform that lets multiplayer studios deploy dedicated servers globally through one REST API.
platforms: Engine-agnostic: any server packaged as a Docker container; Unreal Engine, Unity and Godot named. 21 providers and 200+ datacenters across EU, NA, APAC, LATAM and MEA; bare metal and cloud.
pricing: On-demand $0.07 per vCPU per hour; reserved from $0.035 per vCPU per hour; billed per second with no minimum session length; bandwidth included with no separate egress charge.
key_features: No SDK required in the game server
notable: The FAQ states Gameye was founded in 2017
Named customers include Chivalry 2 (250K CCU at launch) and Clone Drone in the Danger Zone

facts.fact: The Gameye homepage describes it as a game server orchestration platform that deploys dedicated servers globally through one REST API.
The homepage lists on-demand pricing of $0.07 per vCPU per hour and reserved pricing from $0.035 per vCPU per hour, billed per second.
The homepage states Gameye has 21 providers and 200+ datacenters across six continents, and a self-serve Developer Trial is offered.
